prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-13, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-13):
| Current ratio           | 1.44 |
| Retained earnings       | 65,448M |
| Current liabilities     | 36,558M |
| Current assets          | 52,485M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 21,318M |
| Total liabilities       | 77,267M |
| Total assets            | 98,585M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,660M |
| Revenue                 | 19,133M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows solid liquidity (current ratio 1.44) and a substantial equity base relative to retained earnings, but it also carries high leverage (total liabilities about 77.3k vs equity 21.3k, debt-to-equity ~3.6) and a relatively modest EBIT margin. While profitability and retained earnings support credit quality, the elevated leverage and limited interest coverage visibility suggest a cautious investment-grade stance. Overall, BBB+ is justified as a balanced assessment between solvency strength and leverage risk.

DECISION: BBB+
